subject: Retention quote, alternatives, and onboarding feasibility
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@olive-sys.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: counteroffer + onboarding feasibility

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — Oliver and I appreciated the clarity on latency and the routing policy. We need to get internal approvals by end of next week. Before that, procurement has asked for: 1) a written counteroffer to match a competing commercial proposal (lower unit price for text-gen tokens and a 12-month commit), and 2) a concrete plan and estimate for onboarding (timeline, milestones, dedicated SE time, and any credits).

The competitor (named in our internal docs) is offering an apparent 20% lower blended per-token rate, plus a one-time migration credit. Olive is concerned about the migration effort and wants a simple comparison that shows near-term TCO for the first 12 months and an onboarding path that won’t disrupt their Q1 roadmap.

Can you:
- Provide a short, itemized counteroffer we can circulate (preferably with a committed tier + optional onboarding credit).
- Confirm whether Redwood can meet a two-week pilot and a full production cutover in ~6 weeks if we sign a committed package.

I can share the competitor quote under NDA if that helps; procurement is pushing for a written match/near-match by EOW so they can present to the execs.

Thanks — Samir
Procurement Manager, Olive Systems
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@olive-sys.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: counteroffer + onboarding feasibility

Samir —

Appreciate the heads-up and the timeline. We can absolutely put together a short written counteroffer and a realistic onboarding plan. High-level answers up front:
- Pilot: yes — we can stand up a 2-week pilot with a scoped dataset and traffic profile. SE time: 8-12 hours/week during pilot.
- Production cutover in ~6 weeks is feasible for typical integrations (we’ll confirm after scoping).

I’m attaching a short price sheet (Redwood_Pricesheet_Q4_v2.xlsx) and an onboarding outline. If you’re comfortable, please share the competitor quote under NDA and we’ll draft a line-item comparison.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send two counteroffer options (Conservative & Aggressive) with explicit unit rates and a one-time onboarding credit.
2) If either option is promising, we’ll schedule a 30-min pricing alignment call with procurement and engineering this week.

Expect the formal offer in an hour.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: counteroffer + onboarding feasibility (OLV-2026-0917)

Folks — forwarding procurement note from Olive. They’ve received a lower blended rate from a competitor and want a written match or near-match plus onboarding credits. Need quick guidance on concession flexibility for a 12-month committed deal. Key points:
- ARR implied is modest for Redwood scale (~$180k ARR if we assume their current run-rate and a 12-month commit).
- Competitor is ~20% lower on blended per-token; they’re asking for a one-time migration credit.

Proposed two options I plan to share to buy time before the pricing call:
Option A (Conservative): 10% off public list for 12-month commit + $25k onboarding credit (applied as first invoice credit). Reserved capacity tier: Standard (no SLA uplift).
Option B (Aggressive): 20% off list for 12-month commit + $40k onboarding credit + 4 weeks of dedicated SE hours (up to 160 hours), and a production SLA for latency (SLO-based). Requires approval for the credit and the SE time.

Margin note: Option B pushes gross margin below target for the first 6 months but materially increases stickiness and shortens sales cycle.

Can we approve Option B for this account if I get verbal sign-off from procurement? If not, I’ll lead with Option A and ask for targeted counterparty concessions (e.g., shorter commit term or a higher minimum).

Quoted below is Samir’s original note.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: counteroffer + onboarding feasibility (OLV-2026-0917)

Lauren —

Option B is acceptable with a cap: approve up to $35k onboarding credit (not $40k) and up to 120 SE hours (not 160). We need to protect margin and not create an expectation of the larger entitlement across customers. Conditions:
- Onboarding credit runs against first two invoices; unused portion expires at 90 days.
- SE hours must be scheduled and approved by Solutions before provisioning; hours beyond the cap billed at standard rate.

Ask: if you lead with a blended number that is 18% off list (midpoint between A & B) plus the $35k credit and 120 SE hours, will procurement move quickly? If yes I approve.

Also: add a one-page migration checklist (deliverables and timeline) to the offer — that helps Olive quantify the migration risk.

Marcus
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@olive-sys.com>, Olive Systems - procurement@olive-sys.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: counteroffer + onboarding feasibility

Samir —

Thanks for sending the timeline. Per our conversation and internal approvals, attached is a short, itemized counteroffer and a migration checklist that outlines milestones (pilot -> staging -> cutover). High level:

Offer (12-month committed term):
- Blended per-token rate: 18% off public list (blended for text-gen + embeddings as discussed).
- One-time onboarding credit: $35,000 applied to first two invoices (expires 90 days).
- SE support: up to 120 hours of dedicated Solutions Engineer time scoped across pilot and cutover windows (additional hours billable).
- Pilot: 2 weeks (scoped), SE support during pilot included.
- Cutover target: ~6 weeks from SOW signature (dependent on integration scope).
- Reserved capacity: Standard tier (predictable throughput); SLA uplift optional at an incremental cost.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricesheet_Q4_v2.xlsx (line-item rates), Olive_Compare_SOW.pdf (migration checklist + milestones).

If this aligns, next steps:
1) I’ll send a one-page commercial summary for your procurement packet.
2) We can schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to walk the slide and confirm the DocuSign envelope.

If you share the competitor quote under NDA, we’ll map line-by-line to make the tradeoffs explicit for your execs.

Best,
— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachments: Redwood_Pricesheet_Q4_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), Olive_Compare_SOW.pdf (pdf stub)
